title: Organic compounds and hydrocarbons
log: 2026-11-20T12:15:23Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-20T13:37:08Z recheck: the fresh check agreed with the fix, cleared with the fix

match.reason: No bank point teaches the definition of organic compounds as carbon-based and hydrocarbons as carbon-and-hydrogen-only compounds with their sources; the closest, the everyday organic materials point, covers examples rather than this definition, and the family-formulas point goes deeper than Stage 5 needs.

draft.title: Organic compounds and hydrocarbons
card: a compound built around carbon atoms, usually joined to hydrogen and sometimes to oxygen or nitrogen. Sugar, plastic and petrol are all organic compounds.
a compound that contains only carbon and hydrogen atoms. Every hydrocarbon is an organic compound.
A compound that contains carbon is not always organic. Carbon dioxide has carbon, but it is not counted as an organic compound.
Most hydrocarbons come from crude oil and natural gas, which formed from the remains of living things. Living things also make organic compounds, such as the sugars in plants.
draft.remember: Organic compounds are based on carbon. A hydrocarbon has only carbon and hydrogen.

a.q: Which statement correctly describes a hydrocarbon?
opts: It contains only carbon and hydrogen atoms
It contains carbon and oxygen atoms only
It contains carbon, hydrogen and oxygen atoms
It contains hydrogen and oxygen atoms only
a.why: A hydrocarbon is made of carbon and hydrogen and nothing else. A compound with oxygen as well, such as sugar, can be organic, but it is not a hydrocarbon.
a.clue: Look at the name: hydro and carbon.

b.q: A chemist tests three compounds. X has only carbon and hydrogen. Y has carbon, hydrogen and oxygen, and is made by plants. Z is carbon dioxide. Which sorts them correctly?
opts: X is a hydrocarbon, Y is organic but not a hydrocarbon
X and Y are hydrocarbons, Z is organic
Only X is organic, Y and Z are hydrocarbons
X, Y and Z are all organic hydrocarbons
b.why: X has only carbon and hydrogen, so it is a hydrocarbon. Y is based on carbon but has oxygen too, so it is organic but not a hydrocarbon. Z contains carbon but is not counted as organic, so the tempting idea that any carbon compound is organic is wrong.
b.clue: Check which atoms each compound contains, and whether Z counts as organic.

a.best: It contains only carbon and hydrogen atoms

b.best: X is a hydrocarbon, Y is organic but not a hydrocarbon

problems.detail: The question asks which option sorts all three compounds, but the intended answer never says where Z goes. A careful student may reject it as incomplete. It should add 'and Z is not organic'.
The right option stands out. It is the longest and the only one with a qualifier ('organic but not a hydrocarbon'), so a student could pick it without knowing the idea.

Petrol is a mixture of many hydrocarbons, not a single compound. Calling it an organic compound blurs the compound/mixture distinction Stage 5 students learn. Better: 'petrol is made of organic compounds'.

check.summary: The facts on hydrocarbons and organic compounds are right, but the card calls petrol a compound when it is a mixture. In question b, the right option does not place Z and stands out as the longest and only qualified option.
